# Glossary

These are owned working definitions. A term is either assigned to one active
chapter that controls its interface and failure boundary, or marked as a
source-lineage label that carries no normative architectural authority.

## Essential vocabulary

The same word can appear in a plan, a running service, a proof, and an
institutional decision. The object and consumer must travel with it. These
definitions describe the book's engineering vocabulary; domain owners retain
their stricter contracts and evidence limits. Narrative links lead back to
examples in the current independent reader, while the technical links retain
the contract and evidence owner.

| Term | Meaning in this book | What it does not establish | Canonical explanation |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Contract]{#term-contract} | An explicit agreement about an object's identity, inputs, permitted transformations, outputs, obligations, and failure behavior. Domain contracts specialize this common idea. | A schema alone does not enforce the agreement or show that its obligations are adequate. | [Intent-to-Execution Contracts](../chapters/intent-to-execution-contracts.qmd); [Contract in the Human Reader](../reader/index.html#concept-contract) |
| [Lease]{#term-lease} | A scoped decision or reservation for a named holder and object, with a declared lifetime and release, expiry, or revocation rules. Say **effect lease**, **resource allocation lease**, **purpose lease**, or **source admission lease** when their different powers matter. | Holding resources or a source lock does not grant permission to execute an effect. A purpose claim does not establish legitimate information use. | [System Boundaries and Authority](../chapters/system-boundaries-and-authority.qmd); [Resource Economics](../chapters/resource-economics-and-token-budgets.qmd); [Privacy and Information Flow](../chapters/privacy-data-rights-and-information-flow-governance.qmd); [Lease in the Human Reader](../reader/index.html#concept-lease) |
| [Receipt]{#term-receipt} | A retained record of an attempted or reported event, binding the actor, object, method, time, result, and declared limits. A receipt may contain an observation or refer to one. | Receipt existence, signatures, or internal consistency do not make the reported effect true or complete. | [Artifact Graphs, Audit Logs, and Replay](../chapters/artifact-graphs-audit-logs-and-replay.qmd); [Receipt in the Human Reader](../reader/index.html#concept-receipt) |
| [Qualification]{#term-qualification} | A bounded eligibility decision for a particular object, consumer, operating envelope, evidence requirement, and period. Route, instrument, checkpoint, and release qualification are different decisions. | A qualified component does not automatically qualify its replacement, composition, experiment, or deployment. | [Readiness Gates, Residual Escrow, and Quarantine](../chapters/readiness-gates-residual-escrow-and-quarantine.qmd); [Qualification in the Human Reader](../reader/index.html#concept-qualification) |
| [Assurance]{#term-assurance} | An organized argument that named claims are adequately supported for a stated use, with assumptions, evidence, defeaters, and unresolved obligations. | Confidence, argument structure, or a safety-case document does not establish safety or authorize use. | [Safety Cases and Structured Assurance](../chapters/safety-cases-and-structured-assurance.qmd); [Assurance in the Human Reader](../reader/index.html#concept-assurance) |
| [Authority]{#term-authority} | Permission held by a named principal to cause a bounded action or decision under a current policy. **Canonical-source authority** instead names which representation controls a data projection; it is not action permission. | Capability, a high score, an authoritative-looking source, or a consistent record does not create a grant. | [System Boundaries and Authority](../chapters/system-boundaries-and-authority.qmd); [Authority in the Human Reader](../reader/index.html#concept-authority) |
| [Observation]{#term-observation} | A result acquired by a named method from a named target at a stated time, with coverage and missingness limits. It can concern bytes, service state, behavior, or a physical measurement. | A command status is not observation of every consequence. Another process need not be an independent observer if it reads the same upstream report. | [Perception and Observation Trust](../chapters/perception-sensor-fusion-and-observation-trust.qmd); [Artifact Graphs](../chapters/artifact-graphs-audit-logs-and-replay.qmd); [Observation in the Human Reader](../reader/index.html#concept-observation) |
| [Evidence]{#term-evidence} | An observation, artifact, argument, or result considered in relation to a specific proposition through a declared method and maximum inference. Its relevance and strength depend on that relation. | An evidence reference does not independently prove truth, competence, causation, or a stronger support state. | [Evidence States and Claim Discipline](../chapters/evidence-states-and-claim-discipline.qmd); [Evidence in the Human Reader](../reader/index.html#concept-evidence) |
| [Residual]{#term-residual} | A named unresolved obligation, uncertainty, difference, or consequence left relative to a contract or claim, with scope, custody, and a disposition route. | Recording or assigning an owner does not discharge it; accepting a bounded residual does not erase history or grant unrelated authority. | [Readiness Gates and Residual Escrow](../chapters/readiness-gates-residual-escrow-and-quarantine.qmd); [Residual in the Human Reader](../reader/index.html#concept-residual) |
| [Rollback]{#term-rollback} | Restoration of specified controllable state to a declared earlier baseline, checked over a named effect inventory. | Restoring a pointer, file, or checkpoint does not establish reversal of external history, disclosed information, or every downstream effect. | [Governed Operations and Recovery](../chapters/governed-operations-incident-command-and-graceful-degradation.qmd); [Rollback in the Human Reader](../reader/index.html#concept-rollback) |
| [Compensation]{#term-compensation} | A new action that addresses an earlier effect that cannot simply be reversed, retaining both the original event and the response. Its success is scoped and separately observed. | A compensating event is not erasure of the original effect or proof that every affected party or copy has been reached. | [Governed Operations and Recovery](../chapters/governed-operations-incident-command-and-graceful-degradation.qmd); [Compensation in the Human Reader](../reader/index.html#concept-compensation) |
| [Layer]{#term-layer} | A logical responsibility by default. A runtime service is an implementation location; an artifact interface is a data boundary; an institutional role assigns accountable decision power. Name the sense when crossing between them. | A box in a diagram need not be a separate process, model, service, or institution. More boxes do not establish better separation. | [ASI Is a Stack, Not a Model](../chapters/asi-is-a-stack-not-a-model.qmd); [Layer in the Human Reader](../reader/index.html#concept-layer) |

### Three distinctions to keep at a handoff

**Permission and source precedence.** A canonical repository file can control
which configuration is generated while granting no worker permission to edit
or publish it. When a chapter says that canonical state is authoritative, read
that as a rule for resolving projections. When it says that an actor has
authority, identify the principal, permitted effect, target, policy, and time.

**Record, observation, and evidence.** An executor receipt may report that a
release command returned successfully. An observer may read the package
actually served. An evaluator may then use that observation to support a
narrow release-state claim. Those are three relations, even when one file
stores them. Keeping separate processes is useful only to the extent that
their methods and dependencies support the required independence.

**Restored state and repaired consequences.** Moving a branch back can be a
rollback of branch state. A corrective publication can be compensation for
the earlier release. A remaining cached copy can be an owned residual. The
recovery decision must name which of these objects it closed instead of
letting the word *recovered* stand for all of them.

## Architecture and source terms

| Term | Working definition | Owner | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| ASI stack | A proposed substrate-neutral governed architecture of logical responsibility and authority boundaries across alignment, governance, planning, memory, reasoning, execution, routing, compression, evidence, and improvement. A monolithic model, modular service graph, hybrid system, or human/AI process may instantiate the boundaries; the term does not require one model or physical module per layer. | `asi-is-a-stack-not-a-model` [chapter](../chapters/asi-is-a-stack-not-a-model.qmd) | normative architecture definition |
| Noninheritance law | The cross-stack rule that capability does not confer authority, context does not confer belief or permission, plans do not confer effects, receipts do not confer reality, theorems do not confer runtime enforcement, replacements do not inherit qualification, and self-improvement proposals cannot ratify themselves. | `asi-is-a-stack-not-a-model` [chapter](../chapters/asi-is-a-stack-not-a-model.qmd) | opening thesis law; architecture at argument support |
| Governed Transition Calculus | The shared transition shape \(T=(I_s,I_t,A,O,E,R,C,\tau,\Pi)\), separating source and target identity, authority, obligations, evidence, residuals, consumers, expiry or revocation, and rollback, compensation, or retirement. Domain owners add stricter fields; the shape alone proves neither its premises nor runtime enforcement. | `executable-specifications-and-lean-proof-envelope` [chapter](../chapters/executable-specifications-and-lean-proof-envelope.qmd) | shared interface vocabulary; no universal theorem or implementation claim |
| Developmental Intelligence Loop | The governed capability-development lifecycle from curriculum, interaction, prediction error, abstraction, and causal intervention through memory consolidation, proceduralization, skill composition, stabilization, readiness review, and authority-gated promotion. | `governed-model-training-distributed-optimization-and-scaling` [chapter](../chapters/governed-model-training-distributed-optimization-and-scaling.qmd) | cross-owner lifecycle at argument support |
| Minimum trusted kernel | The smallest explicit trust budget over identity, time, authority, policy, context resolution, artifact custody, observation, evaluation, sandboxing, rollback, and release whose failure can invalidate a governed transition. | `security-kernel-and-digital-scifs` [chapter](../chapters/security-kernel-and-digital-scifs.qmd) | trust-minimization target; no secure implementation claim |
| Bounded liveness | The requirement that admitted tasks, residuals, quarantines, and review loops reach finite owned dispositions while useful throughput, false blocking, latency, human time, compute, recovery, residual burden, and governance cost remain visible beside safety. | `security-kernel-and-digital-scifs` [chapter](../chapters/security-kernel-and-digital-scifs.qmd) | joint safety/usefulness target |
| P0–P6 semantic depth | A non-promotional classification of formal or executable reach: P0 record shape, P1 finite route, P2 reachable witness, P3 implementation binding, P4 cross-component safety, P5 liveness or recovery, and P6 empirical binding to a named observation contract. | `executable-specifications-and-lean-proof-envelope` [chapter](../chapters/executable-specifications-and-lean-proof-envelope.qmd) | proof-scope organization; levels must be earned independently |
| Alignment and constitution | The layer that constrains admissible goals, values, self-modification, and human-agency requirements. | `constitutional-alignment-substrate` [chapter](../chapters/constitutional-alignment-substrate.qmd) | owned interface definition |
| Stable Capability Field | A stable capability boundary with replaceable implementations, bounded authority, qualification evidence, and rollback rules. | `stable-capability-fields` [chapter](../chapters/stable-capability-fields.qmd) | owned interface definition |
| PlanForge | A source-lineage label for compiling goals into governed task graphs, dependencies, budgets, and replanning triggers; the active interface owner is Planning as a Control Layer. | `planning-as-a-control-layer` [chapter](../chapters/planning-as-a-control-layer.qmd) | lineage label; not a separate normative layer |
| Virtual Context Memory | A source-lineage label for governed context materialization from durable sources; the active interface owner is the Virtual Context ABI. | `virtual-context-abi` [chapter](../chapters/virtual-context-abi.qmd) | lineage label; not a separate normative layer |
| Talos | A source-lineage label for typed jobs, execution, artifacts, permissions, audit, and replay; active ownership is split across the named execution chapters. | `labor-os-and-typed-jobs` [chapter](../chapters/labor-os-and-typed-jobs.qmd) | lineage label; not a separate normative layer |
| Spinoza | A source-lineage label for claim verification and belief revision; active ownership is split between Claim Ledgers and Proof-Carrying Claims. | `spinoza-verification-and-proof-carrying-claims` [chapter](../chapters/spinoza-verification-and-proof-carrying-claims.qmd) | lineage label; not a separate normative layer |
| MoECOT | A source-lineage label for modular orchestration with specialist cores, readiness gates, ledgers, and replay. | `routing-heads-and-specialist-cores` [chapter](../chapters/routing-heads-and-specialist-cores.qmd) | lineage label; not independent implementation evidence |
| Octopus Router | A source-lineage label for dynamically selecting bounded specialist arms or cores. | `routing-heads-and-specialist-cores` [chapter](../chapters/routing-heads-and-specialist-cores.qmd) | lineage label; routing interface owned by chapter |
| Ratcheting Modular Intelligence | A source-lineage doctrine based on benchmark frontiers, residual escrow, regression preservation, and verified module promotion. | `benchmark-ratchets-and-anti-goodhart-evidence` [chapter](../chapters/benchmark-ratchets-and-anti-goodhart-evidence.qmd) | lineage label; not an independent evidence class |
| Compact Generative Systems | The compression owner for selecting the smallest adequate generative or governing structure without hiding residual complexity. | `compact-generative-systems-and-residual-honesty` [chapter](../chapters/compact-generative-systems-and-residual-honesty.qmd) | owned interface definition |
| RankFold / NeuralFold | A compression source-lineage label for low-rank residual coding, functional preprocessing, and fallback routing. | `rankfold-neuralfold-and-artifact-compression` [chapter](../chapters/rankfold-neuralfold-and-artifact-compression.qmd) | lineage label; mechanism claims require separate evidence |
| Functional precision | The minimum numerical and representational detail needed by a complete executable implementation to preserve named behavior under a declared domain, metric vector, tail rule, resource envelope, and fallback policy. It is contract-relative and not a universal bits-per-weight property. | `rankfold-neuralfold-and-artifact-compression` [chapter](../chapters/rankfold-neuralfold-and-artifact-compression.qmd) | owned compression-interface definition; no optimality or preservation result |
| Precision Contract | A versioned contract binding protected behavior, domain and exclusions, metrics and thresholds, confidence, physical resources, escalation, fallback, and exact reference, transformed, decoder, runtime, platform, and evaluator identities. | `rankfold-neuralfold-and-artifact-compression` [chapter](../chapters/rankfold-neuralfold-and-artifact-compression.qmd) | owned admission artifact; contract selection and satisfaction require separate evidence |
| Precision field | A governed allocation of numerical precision across layers, channels, directions, tokens, tasks, uncertainty states, and consequence classes, optionally using ordered residual planes and a conservative route. | `rankfold-neuralfold-and-artifact-compression` [chapter](../chapters/rankfold-neuralfold-and-artifact-compression.qmd) | design-rationale resource allocation; no routing advantage claim |
| Precision Certificate | A scoped, expiring receipt that binds one transformed executable package to its protected contract, evidence, cost ledger, route, fallback, limits, platform, and revocation state. | `readiness-gates-residual-escrow-and-quarantine` [chapter](../chapters/readiness-gates-residual-escrow-and-quarantine.qmd) | readiness input only; not optimality, safety, support, or deployment authority |
| BBVCA | A generate-verify-repair source-lineage label using seeded local laws, bounded search, and residual tracking. | `compact-generative-systems-and-residual-honesty` [chapter](../chapters/compact-generative-systems-and-residual-honesty.qmd) | lineage label; mechanism claims require separate evidence |
| Artifact graph | A traceable graph of produced objects, source handles, jobs, claims, evidence records, projections, revocations, and replay grades. | `artifact-graphs-audit-logs-and-replay` [chapter](../chapters/artifact-graphs-audit-logs-and-replay.qmd) | owned interface definition |
| Claim ledger | A structured lifecycle record of claims, support states, sources, uncertainty, contradiction links, revisions, and review status. | `claim-ledgers-and-belief-revision` [chapter](../chapters/claim-ledgers-and-belief-revision.qmd) | owned interface definition |
| Context packet | An active bounded context materialization supplied to an agent or job, including source handles, summaries, authority labels, and adequacy status; it is not durable memory. | `virtual-context-abi` [chapter](../chapters/virtual-context-abi.qmd) | owned interface definition |
| Proof-carrying summary | A bounded summary carrying provenance and checks sufficient to audit the stated fidelity obligation without proving the broader source claim. | `spinoza-verification-and-proof-carrying-claims` [chapter](../chapters/spinoza-verification-and-proof-carrying-claims.qmd) | owned verification artifact definition |
| Authority ceiling | The maximum action authority a principal, layer, field, tool, or implementation may exercise under a named grant and policy state. | `system-boundaries-and-authority` [chapter](../chapters/system-boundaries-and-authority.qmd) | owned invariant definition |
| Readiness gate | An evidence, authority, regression, and residual checkpoint that must pass before a capability or artifact may enter a stronger lifecycle state. | `readiness-gates-residual-escrow-and-quarantine` [chapter](../chapters/readiness-gates-residual-escrow-and-quarantine.qmd) | owned lifecycle definition |
| Residual escrow | A visible owned ledger of unresolved failures, uncertainty, debt, or residual complexity left by a route, compression, benchmark, or release decision. | `readiness-gates-residual-escrow-and-quarantine` [chapter](../chapters/readiness-gates-residual-escrow-and-quarantine.qmd) | owned lifecycle definition |
| Benchmark ratchet | A governed benchmark lifecycle that preserves floors, negative cases, provenance, contamination controls, and residuals while moving an evaluation frontier. | `benchmark-ratchets-and-anti-goodhart-evidence` [chapter](../chapters/benchmark-ratchets-and-anti-goodhart-evidence.qmd) | owned evidence-interface definition |

| Optimizer Policy Card | The executable optimizer identity for one run: family and implementation, parameterization, eligible parameter groups and fallback, state and precision, update equation, schedule or averaging state, decay, clipping, stabilizers, preconditioner or curvature cadence, approximation, batch/topology semantics, tuning budget, rescue ladder, checkpoint state, and nonclaims. | `governed-model-training-distributed-optimization-and-scaling` [chapter](../chapters/governed-model-training-distributed-optimization-and-scaling.qmd) | owned training-policy definition; an optimizer family name alone is insufficient |
| Optimizer family | A class of update mechanisms sharing a broad information or geometry choice—such as coordinate adaptation, tensor preconditioning, curvature approximation, sign updates, orthogonalized matrix updates, or schedule/averaging policy. A family does not specify a runnable configuration or imply superiority. | `governed-model-training-distributed-optimization-and-scaling` [chapter](../chapters/governed-model-training-distributed-optimization-and-scaling.qmd) | taxonomy term; no evidence or selection authority |
| Method-specific rescue | A prospectively bounded debugging and tuning opportunity tailored to an optimizer's known implementation requirements, applied before a failed arm may support a negative inference and charged to its tuning budget. | `governed-model-training-distributed-optimization-and-scaling` [chapter](../chapters/governed-model-training-distributed-optimization-and-scaling.qmd) | competence-gate definition; cannot use held-out outcomes |

| Activation policy candidate | A separately qualified proposal to observe or intervene on named internal states for a bounded purpose, population, model identity, and monitor window. | Qualified branch packet | A model-, observation-, checkpoint-, horizon-, intervention-, calibration-, disagreement-, planner-, and authority-bound record for an imagined consequence. | Reality-residual record | A preserved comparison between a prior model-relative prediction and an independently admitted later observation, with materiality, attribution limits, affected descendants, and a required re-estimation, replan, fallback, review, or safe-hold route. | `governed-world-models-and-reality-grounding` [chapter](../chapters/governed-world-models-and-reality-grounding.qmd) | owned prediction-to-observation reconciliation definition |
| Human control-envelope packet | A task-, controller-, evidence-, representation-, workload-, time-, authority-, intervention-, conflict-, privacy-, responsibility-, and lifecycle-bound record used to decide whether a nominal human role may proceed to bounded review, needs added capacity or reduced autonomy, or must safe-hold. It cannot infer internal state, assign moral responsibility, grant effect or support authority, or certify meaningful control. | `human-factors-and-meaningful-control-in-oversight` [chapter](../chapters/human-factors-and-meaningful-control-in-oversight.qmd) | owned operator-capacity interface definition |

| Ceremonial approval | An approval event for which one or more necessary control conditions—relevant evidence, comprehension opportunity, authority, time, viable alternatives, effective intervention, or reachable safe state—were absent or unresolved. The label is a bounded operational diagnosis, not a judgment of the person. | `human-factors-and-meaningful-control-in-oversight` [chapter](../chapters/human-factors-and-meaningful-control-in-oversight.qmd) | owned human-control failure definition |
